$comment: Chapter 0 — The Ghost of Shapla-1 (tutorial, ~3 min). Investigate the old failure; learn to read a budget; Kabir's confession.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Nine years ago, our first satellite went dark over the Bay of Bengal. They say bad luck.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Tonight, the archive room hums. Kabir-bhai unlocks the old telemetry with a key he keeps on the same ring as his house keys.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Every engineer visits this room eventually. Come. The wreck of Shapla-1 still has something to teach.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Think of a spacecraft as a rickshaw. Mass is passengers. Power is the puller's legs. Panels are how much he can eat. The battery is what he saved for the hill.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Shapla-1's puller had weak legs and no savings. The panels gave less than the instruments ate. In eclipse, the battery drained to zero. Everything died in the dark.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The debrief board glows. Three clues float in the amber light: the battery, the panels, the instrument power draw.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Tell me what killed her. What do you see first?

choices.text: The battery was too small for the eclipse.
The instruments drew more than the panels made.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Sharp. Forty watt-hours, and the night side eats more than that each orbit. But there is a deeper cut.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Right — day and night, the instruments ate more than the panels made. The battery only delayed the funeral. But there is a deeper cut.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: When I signed her power budget, the numbers said: enough. Not comfortable. Not with margin. Enough — like a rickshaw puller fed exactly one meal a day.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: A fuse blows, a storm delays a pass, an instrument runs hot. Luck finds the crack every time. I left the crack. I signed it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: He looks at the shapla emblem on the old mission patch for a long moment. The rain keeps time on the window.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Luck is just margin you didn't plan. Write that somewhere you will not lose it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The archive light dims. Somewhere upstairs, a weather radar paints a slow white spiral in the Bay of Bengal. Tomorrow, there will be no time for ghosts.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Come. If we are going to stare down a cyclone, you should meet the rest of the family.
